literal: Eastern Capital Circuit
idiomatic: Eastern Capital Circuit

literal: Eastern Capital Liaoyang Prefecture was originally Chaoxian territory.
idiomatic: Liaoyang Prefecture of the Eastern Capital was ancient Chaoxian land.

literal: King Wu of Zhou released Jizi from prison; Jizi went to Chaoxian and was enfeoffed there.
idiomatic: When King Wu of Zhou freed Jizi from captivity, Jizi withdrew to Chaoxian and received investiture there.

literal: He made the Eight Precepts, honored ritual and righteousness, enriched farming and sericulture; outer gates were not shut and men did not steal.
idiomatic: He promulgated the Eight Precepts, exalted ritual and right conduct, and promoted agriculture and silk—outer gates stood unbarred and theft vanished.

literal: It was transmitted through more than forty generations.
idiomatic: The line endured more than forty generations.

literal: Under Yan it belonged to Zhenfan and Chaoxian; officials were first appointed and barriers built.
idiomatic: Under Yan it fell under Zhenfan and Chaoxian; the dynasty first posted officials and raised frontier barriers.

literal: Under Qin it belonged to Liaodong outer frontier.
idiomatic: Under Qin it lay within Liaodong's outer marches.

literal: At the beginning of Han it was empty land of the Yan man Man.
idiomatic: In early Han it was vacant territory once held by the Yan commander Man.

literal: In the third year of Emperor Wu's Yuanfeng era, Chaoxian was fixed as four commanderies: Zhenfan, Lintun, Lelang, and Xuantu.
idiomatic: In Yuanfeng year 3 Emperor Wu organized Chaoxian into four commanderies—Zhenfan, Lintun, Lelang, and Xuantu.

literal: Later Han moved between Qing and You two provinces and Liaodong and Xuantu two commanderies; changes were not constant.
idiomatic: Under Later Han it shifted between the Qing and You provinces and between Liaodong and Xuantu—its administrative lines were never stable.

literal: At the end of Han it was seized by Gongsun Du and transmitted to his son Kang;
idiomatic: In late Han Gongsun Du seized it and passed control to his son Kang;

literal: grandson Yuan styled himself King of Yan, era name Shaohan; Wei destroyed him.
idiomatic: his grandson Yuan declared himself King of Yan with era Shaohan, until Wei overthrew him.

literal: Jin fell to Goryeo; later it returned to Murong Chui;
idiomatic: Jin lost the region to Goryeo, which later yielded to Murong Chui;

literal: son Bao installed the Goguryeo king An as Ping Prefecture governor to dwell there.
idiomatic: Bao installed the Goguryeo king An as governor of Ping Prefecture and settled him there.

literal: Northern Wei Emperor Taiwu sent envoys to his seat at Pyongyang; Liao's Eastern Capital originally derives from this.
idiomatic: Northern Wei Emperor Taiwu dispatched envoys to Pyongyang—the Liao Eastern Capital traces to this seat.

literal: Tang Emperor Gaozong pacified Goryeo and here established the Andong Protectorate;
idiomatic: When Tang Gaozong conquered Goryeo he placed the Andong Protectorate here;

literal: later it came into the possession of the Great Clan of Bohai.
idiomatic: later the Great Clan of Bohai held it.

literal: The Great Clan first held Dongmou Mountain east of Yilou.
idiomatic: The clan first secured Dongmou Mountain east of Yilou.

literal: In Empress Wu's Wansui Tongtian era, pressed by Khitan Jinzhong's revolt, one Qiqi Zhongxiang crossed the Liao River to hold himself secure; Wu enfeoffed him Duke of Zhen.
idiomatic: During Empress Wu's Wansui Tongtian reign, harried by Khitan Jinzhong, Qiqi Zhongxiang crossed the Liao to fortify himself and was enfeoffed Duke of Zhen.

literal: His son Zuorong built a capital, styled himself King Zhen, swallowed the north sea coast, with territory five thousand li and armies in the hundreds of thousands.
idiomatic: Zuorong founded a capital, took the title King Zhen, absorbed the northern seacoast—five thousand li of ground and armies numbering hundreds of thousands.

literal: Zhongzong granted his capital the name Hohan Prefecture and enfeoffed him Prince of Bohai.
idiomatic: Zhongzong named his capital Hohan Prefecture and made him Prince of Bohai.

literal: Through twelve generations to Yizhen, he usurped an era title, imitated palace building, had five capitals, fifteen prefectures, and sixty-two zhou—an eastern flourishing state.
idiomatic: By the twelfth generation Yizhen adopted reign titles, modeled palaces, and maintained five capitals, fifteen fu, and sixty-two zhou—a great power of the eastern sea.

literal: Hohan Prefecture is the old Pyongyang city, styled Central Capital Xiande Prefecture.
idiomatic: Hohan Prefecture was the old Pyongyang, called Central Capital Xiande Prefecture.

literal: 1 Taizu founded the state, attacked Bohai, seized Hohan city, captured its king Dainiezhi, made an Eastern Dan state, and installed Crown Prince Tuyu as Renhuang King to rule it.
idiomatic: First: Taizu founded the dynasty, attacked Bohai, took Hohan city, captured King Dainiezhi, established Eastern Dan, and set Crown Prince Tuyu as Renhuang King to govern it.

literal: In Shence year 4 he repaired the old Liaoyang walls, used Bohai and Han households to build Dongping Commandery as a defense prefecture.
idiomatic: In Shence year 4 he restored old Liaoyang, settled Bohai and Han households there, and created Dongping Commandery as a defense prefecture.

literal: 2 In Tianxian year 3 Eastern Dan people were moved to dwell there; it was promoted to Nanjing.
idiomatic: Second: In Tianxian year 3 Eastern Dan subjects were relocated there and the seat was raised to Nanjing.

literal: The city was named Tianfu; 3 it was three zhang high, with towers and parapets, circumference thirty li.
idiomatic: The city bore the name Tianfu; third, its walls stood three zhang high with towers and parapets, thirty li in circuit.

literal: Eight gates: east called Yingyang, southeast Shaoyang, south Longyuan, southwest Xiande, west Dashun, northwest Daliao, north Huaiyuan, northeast Anyuan.
idiomatic: Eight gates: east Yingyang, southeast Shaoyang, south Longyuan, southwest Xiande, west Dashun, northwest Daliao, north Huaiyuan, northeast Anyuan.

literal: The palace city lay in the northeast corner, three zhang high, with fighting towers; south were three gates, grand with towered pavilions; at the four corners were corner towers, each two li apart.
idiomatic: The palace quarter stood northeast, three zhang high with fighting towers; three southern gates rose with towered pavilions; corner towers at the four angles stood two li apart.

literal: North of the palace wall was the Abdication Emperor's portrait hall.
idiomatic: North of the palace wall stood the Abdication Emperor's portrait hall.

literal: Within the Great Inner two halls were built; palace women were not installed—only Inner Secretariat deputy commissioners and judging officials guarded it.
idiomatic: The Great Inner held two halls without palace women—only Inner Secretariat deputies and judging officials kept watch.

literal: The Great Eastern Dan State New Nanjing stele inscription stood south of the palace gate.
idiomatic: A stele inscription for the Great Eastern Dan State's new Nanjing stood south of the palace gate.

literal: The outer city was called Han City, divided into south and north markets with a viewing tower between;
idiomatic: The outer city, called Han City, split into south and north markets with a viewing tower at the center;

literal: morning gatherings were in the south market, evening in the north market.
idiomatic: morning trade gathered in the south market, evening in the north.

literal: West of the streets was Jinde Temple;
idiomatic: West of the avenues stood Jinde Temple;

literal: Dabei Temple;
idiomatic: Dabei Temple;

literal: Imperial Son-in-Law Temple, where the iron banner pole stood;
idiomatic: Imperial Son-in-Law Temple, site of the iron banner pole;

literal: Zhao the Ascetic Temple;
idiomatic: the Temple of Zhao the Ascetic;

literal: Regent Yamen;
idiomatic: the Regent Yamen;

literal: Households Bureau;
idiomatic: the Households Bureau;

literal: Military Patrol Office—with more than a thousand Guihua Camp troops; fugitives from Hebei were all registered here.
idiomatic: the Military Patrol Office—over a thousand Guihua Camp troops; Hebei fugitives were enrolled here.

literal: East to North Wuluhuke four hundred li, south to seaside Tieshan eight hundred sixty li, west to Wangping County estuary three hundred sixty li, north to Yilou County and Fan River two hundred seventy li.
idiomatic: It reached four hundred li east to North Wuluhuke, eight hundred sixty li south to seaside Tieshan, three hundred sixty li west to Wangping County's estuary, and two hundred seventy li north to Yilou County and the Fan River.

literal: East, west, and south embraced the sea.
idiomatic: East, west, and south faced the sea.

literal: The Liao River issued from the northeast pass as the Fan River, flowed southwest as the great mouth, and entered the sea;
idiomatic: The Liao River left the northeast pass as the Fan River, ran southwest as the great mouth, and entered the sea;

literal: the Dongliang River flowed west from the eastern mountains, joined the Hun River as the small mouth, met the Liao River and entered the sea—also called Crown Prince River, also Daliang River;
idiomatic: the Dongliang River descended west from the eastern hills, united with the Hun as the small mouth, and with the Liao reached the sea—also Crown Prince River or Daliang River;

literal: the Hun River lay between the Dongliang and Fan rivers;
idiomatic: the Hun lay between the Dongliang and Fan rivers;

literal: the Sha River issued from the southeast mountains and flowed northwest, passing through Gai Prefecture into the sea.
idiomatic: the Sha River ran northwest from the southeast hills through Gai Prefecture to the sea.

literal: There was the Pu River;
idiomatic: There were the Pu River;

literal: Qing River;
idiomatic: the Qing River;

literal: and Ni River—also called Taro Marsh, for the many taro grasses in its waters;
idiomatic: and the Ni River, also Taro Marsh from the taro grasses along its course;

literal: Imperial Encampment Mountain—when Tang Taizong campaigned against Goryeo he encamped on its summit for days and carved stone to record merit; commonly called Hand Mountain, for palm and finger shapes on the flat summit stone; a spring issued within it and never failed.
idiomatic: Imperial Encampment Mountain: Tang Taizong campaigned against Goryeo, encamped on the summit for days, and carved a merit stele—folk called it Hand Mountain for palm-shaped marks on the flat rock; an inexhaustible spring rose within.

literal: There were also Mingwang Mountain and Baishi Mountain, also called Heng Mountain.
idiomatic: Mingwang Mountain and Baishi Mountain—also Heng Mountain—lay nearby.

literal: In Tianxian year 13 Nanjing was changed to the Eastern Capital and the prefecture called Liaoyang.
idiomatic: In Tianxian year 13 Nanjing became the Eastern Capital and the prefecture was named Liaoyang.

literal: Households 40,604.
idiomatic: 40,604 households.

literal: It governed eighty-seven prefectures, fu, armies, and cities.
idiomatic: It ruled eighty-seven prefectures, fu, armies, and fortified towns.

literal: 4 Governing nine counties:
idiomatic: Fourth: nine counties:

literal: Liaoyang County.
idiomatic: Liaoyang County.

literal: Originally Bohai state Jinde County land.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Jinde County territory.

literal: Hanshui County—Goryeo changed it to Goguryeo County, Bohai to Changle County.
idiomatic: Hanshui County: Goryeo renamed it Goguryeo County; Bohai called it Changle County.

literal: Households 1,500.
idiomatic: 1,500 households.

literal: Xianxiang County.
idiomatic: Xianxiang County.

literal: Originally Han Liaodui County; Bohai made it Yongfeng County.
idiomatic: Originally Han Liaodui County; under Bohai, Yongfeng County.

literal: The Immortals' Traditions says: "The immortal Bai Zhongli could refine divine elixir and transmute gold to save the people."
idiomatic: Immortals' Traditions records: "The immortal Bai Zhongli refined divine elixir and transmuted gold to succor the people."

literal: " Households 1,500.
idiomatic: " 1,500 households.

literal: Heye County.
idiomatic: Heye County.

literal: Originally Han Jujiu County land; Bohai made it Jishan County.
idiomatic: Originally Han Jujiu County; under Bohai, Jishan County.

literal: Long ago Ding Lingwei dwelt here; after a thousand years away he became a crane and returned, alighting on a memorial pillar, painting the tablet:
idiomatic: Ding Lingwei once lived here; a millennium later he returned as a crane and perched on a memorial pillar, inscribing the tablet:

literal: "There is a bird, there is a bird—Ding Lingwei; a thousand years from home, now returning; though walls and towers stand, the people are not—why not learn immortality and leave tombs in rows?"
idiomatic: "A bird, a bird—Ding Lingwei; gone a thousand years, now home again; the city stands but men are gone—why not seek immortality rather than mounded graves?"

literal: " Households 1,200.
idiomatic: " 1,200 households.

literal: Ximu County.
idiomatic: Ximu County.

literal: Originally Han Wangping County land; Bohai made it Huashan County.
idiomatic: Originally Han Wangping County; under Bohai, Huashan County.

literal: Households 1,000.
idiomatic: 1,000 households.

literal: Zimeng County.
idiomatic: Zimeng County.

literal: Originally Han Loufang County land.
idiomatic: Originally Han Loufang County territory.

literal: 5 Later the Funie state set up Dongping Prefecture governing Meng Prefecture Zimeng County.
idiomatic: Fifth: later Funie established Dongping Prefecture, governing Meng Prefecture's Zimeng County.

literal: Later it was moved to Liao city and merged into Huangling County.
idiomatic: It was later moved to Liao city and merged into Huangling County.

literal: Bohai again made it Zimeng County.
idiomatic: Bohai restored the name Zimeng County.

literal: Households 1,000.
idiomatic: 1,000 households.

literal: Xingliao County.
idiomatic: Xingliao County.

literal: Originally Han Pingguo County land; Bohai changed it to Changning County.
idiomatic: Originally Han Pingguo County; Bohai renamed it Changning County.

literal: In Tang Yuanhe era Bohai King Da Renxiu pacified Silla in the south and reduced northern tribes, opening commanderies and counties—thus fixing the present name.
idiomatic: In Tang's Yuanhe reign Bohai King Da Renxiu subdued Silla in the south and northern tribes, establishing commanderies and counties and fixing the present name.

literal: Households 1,000.
idiomatic: 1,000 households.

literal: Sushen County.
idiomatic: Sushen County.

literal: Established with Bohai households.
idiomatic: Settled with Bohai households.

literal: Guiren County.
idiomatic: Guiren County.

literal: Shunhua County.
idiomatic: Shunhua County.

literal: Kai Prefecture, Zhenguo Army, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Kai Prefecture (Zhenguo Army), military commissioner.

literal: Originally Mo land; Goryeo made it Qing Prefecture; Bohai made it Eastern Capital Longyuan Prefecture.
idiomatic: Originally Mo territory; Goryeo made Qing Prefecture; Bohai made it Eastern Capital Longyuan Prefecture.

literal: It had palaces.
idiomatic: Palaces stood there.

literal: It superintended Qing, Yan, Mu, and He four prefectures.
idiomatic: It oversaw Qing, Yan, Mu, and He prefectures.

literal: Former counties six: Longyuan, Yong'an, Wushan, Bigu, Xiongshan, and Baiyang—all abolished.
idiomatic: Six former counties—Longyuan, Yong'an, Wushan, Bigu, Xiongshan, and Baiyang—were all abolished.

literal: Stacked stone made the walls, twenty li in circuit.
idiomatic: Walls of stacked stone ran twenty li around.

literal: Tang Xue Rengui campaigned against Goryeo and fought their great general Wen Shamen at Xiongshan, capturing marksmen at Shicheng—this is that place.
idiomatic: When Tang Xue Rengui attacked Goryeo he battled Wen Shamen at Xiongshan and seized marksmen at Shicheng—this was the site.

literal: Taizu pacified Bohai and moved its people to great tribal settlements; the city was then abandoned.
idiomatic: Taizu conquered Bohai and relocated its people to great tribal settlements, abandoning the city.

literal: Shengzong returned from campaigning Goryeo, 6 toured the city foundations, and restored them further.
idiomatic: Shengzong, returning from a Goryeo campaign, sixth: inspected the foundations and repaired the walls anew.

literal: In Kaitai year 3 more than a thousand households from Shuang and Han prefectures were moved to fill it; it was styled Kaifeng Prefecture Kaiyuan Army, military commissioner;
idiomatic: Kaitai year 3 brought over a thousand households from Shuang and Han prefectures; it became Kaifeng Prefecture (Kaiyuan Army) with a military commissioner;

literal: renamed Zhenguo Army.
idiomatic: then renamed Zhenguo Army.

literal: Subordinate to the Eastern Capital regent; military affairs belonged to the Eastern Capital army command.
idiomatic: It answered to the Eastern Capital regent; military affairs to the Eastern Capital army command.

literal: Governing three prefectures and one county:
idiomatic: Three prefectures, one county:

literal: Kaiyuan County.
idiomatic: Kaiyuan County.
